subject: Renewal: options to stabilize price via staged prepay and ramp
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@greenlane.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Park <jordan.park@greenlane.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 11:32:00 -0700
Subject: Upcoming renewal and question on locking rates

Soojin —

Our annual contract with Redwood is up for renewal at the end of April and we're seeing pricing increases industry-wide. Before we start internal approvals, I wanted to check if there are straightforward options to lock current unit pricing for Greenlane — we prefer predictability over moving models. Specifically: can multi-year prepay (or an upfront commitment) be structured so we avoid step-up pricing mid-term?

High level: our usage this year was ~1.4B tokens/month average; depending on the deal we can consider a 2-year commit with a modest ramp in year 1. Budget owners want clarity on discount tiers and any commitments for minimums/commitment credit mechanics.

Would you be able to share a couple of concrete structures (one-year annual prepay, two-year with staged ramp, and any hybrid) and the typical discount ranges? Also flag any early termination or migration clauses we should be aware of.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if easier.

—Alex
Alex Turner
Head of ML Platform, Greenlane Analytics
alex.turner@greenlane.ai

From: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@greenlane.ai>

Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal and question on locking rates

Alex —

Thanks for the note and helpful context. We can absolutely design a structure to prioritize price stability while giving Greenlane flexibility on ramp. Attached is a short term sheet and three model options (see Redwood_PrePay_TermSheet_v1.pdf):

1) Annual prepay (1-year): up-front purchase for 12 months at a discounted per-token rate. Best for teams that want simple budgeting and no multi-year commitment. Typical discount: 5–8% relative to monthly pay-as-you-go.

2) Two-year staged prepay (recommended for price lock): 2-year commitment with an agreed ramp schedule. Example structure we often propose: 12 months at 60% of committed capacity (to accommodate conservative first-year forecasting), then 100% in year 2. Multi-year discount applied on top of annual prepay (illustrative: 6% in year 1, 8–12% in year 2 depending on size). This locks per-token list pricing for the full 24 months.

3) Hybrid (upfront + top-up): initial upfront covers baseline (e.g., 50% of expected usage) with a credit mechanic for top-ups invoiced monthly at a slightly higher rate. Useful if you want a predictable base plus optional elasticity.

Mechanics and notes:
- Commitment credit: unused committed units convert to account-level credit that can be consumed within the contract term (not refundable).
- Early termination: standard pro-rated return policy with a small fee; for multi-year deals we typically offer an early-termination schedule tied to remaining committed value.
- SLA / migration: we'll include an SLA credits matrix; if Greenlane needs stronger exit protections we can add migration assistance clauses (professional services scope).

Next steps I suggest: I can circulate a draft term sheet and a 2-yr numeric example based on your 1.4B tokens/mo profile. Vivek/Rishi — can you confirm we can offer the 2-year staged structure with the discount bands above and the credit mechanics? Marissa — want you on the thread for renewal and CS handoff.

I attached the term sheet draft for your review. If it looks reasonable I can get our legal/finance teams to produce redlines for DocuSign. Happy to book a 30-min call this week to walk through numbers.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Principal Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

Subject: Re: Upcoming renewal and question on locking rates

Soojin —

Thanks for the clear options. From a commercial standpoint I endorse the two-year staged prepay as the primary path — it aligns our incentives on price stability and predictable consumption. A few internal asks before we present numbers:

- Finance (Rishi): confirm discount bands we can commit to without further approval. I think we can do 6% year 1 / 10% year 2 for the committed base at the volumes Alex mentioned, but confirm.
- CS (Marissa): highlight what migration assistance / early ramp support we can guarantee if Greenlane needs to accelerate usage.
- Legal: we'll need a lightweight early termination ladder.

If those checkboxes are green, I suggest we push the 2-yr example with numeric figures (committed token counts, dollars saved vs PAYG, and effective per-token price) and an attached DocuSign-ready term sheet. I'll also flag that we can include a 60-day price protection window after signature.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Growth — Redwood Inference

Jordan / Alex —

Appreciate the clear asks — that helps. Quick summary of what we can offer and the proposal I will send as a redline-ready doc:

- Reallocation: yes — unused committed units can be reallocated across Greenlane BU wallets under the same master account. We'll add an administrative clause and process in the term sheet.
- Ramp: happy to move year-1 to 70% of committed capacity (instead of 60%) as you requested.
- Discounts: proposed committed-base pricing (illustrative for discussion):
  • Year 1 (70% baseline): 8% discount vs PAYG on the committed baseline
  • Year 2 (100% baseline): 12% discount vs PAYG on the committed baseline
  • Additional top-ups: paid monthly at PAYG - 2% (small premium to the committed baseline).
- SLA: we can commit to 99.9% availability for serving endpoints in the Dedicated offering and include SLA credits as documented in SLA_Credits_Matrix.xlsx. For Hosted API we can include similar credits; migration assistance for higher availability tiers is negotiable.
- PO flow: we accept Greenlane's PO template; legal will add standard commercial terms and the early termination ladder.

I attached the SLA credits matrix and will circulate a DocuSign-ready term sheet that reflects the reallocation clause and the 70% ramp. Proposed next steps:

1) I'll send the redline-ready term sheet (DocuSign link included) by Monday.
2) If the term sheet is acceptable, procurement signs the PO and we countersign.
3) Marissa and CS will schedule a 1-week onboarding ramp assistance plan once the contract is active.

If this plan sounds OK I can lock the pricing protection window (60 days) from signature and route to legal/finance for final signoff.

Best — talk soon,
